take_homes: An agent can read a folder of my own documents and give a cited answer. I can check the citations myself, which is more than a slide lets me do.
Adding a new source made the notes tighter, and I saw that on my screen. It stays honest only if I keep correcting it, and it knows only what has been written down.
The setup is plain files, and the agent only drafts. Nothing is sent without me, which is the guardrail I'd want.

monday.move: Run the daily risk scan on the partner-pricing memory I built, and read the output for three mornings without changing anything.
monday.who: me alone, with no colleagues involved yet
monday.stop_condition: If after three mornings it only tells me things I already knew, I drop it.
monday.blocker: A calendar full of the last programme's steering groups, and the memory is still thin on internal numbers.

misconception.why: Wait-and-see still looks sensible for the hype. But I watched new sources make the notes tighter, which I couldn't do in chat, and the files outlive any model change. This one differs from agile because I could test it myself. I'm not converted yet.

one_line: Unlike the last three programmes, I tested this one myself and it worked, though the compounding slogans could go.
